about: Bonfiglioli Transmissions makes gear motors, gearboxes and drive systems in India for industrial automation, off-highway mobility (excavators, cranes) and wind turbine (yaw and pitch drives) customers. It is a wholly owned subsidiary of Italy's Bonfiglioli S.p.A. and runs three plants (two in Tamil Nadu, one in Maharashtra) that built about 341,133 units in 2025. It served over 930 direct customers in H1 2026.
sector: Industrial Machinery - Power Transmission (Gearboxes and Drives)

promoters.background: Wholly owned by Bonfiglioli S.p.A. (Italy, group revenue EUR 1,172.94 million in 2025), which is controlled by the Bonfiglioli family through BON-FI S.r.l. Average cost of acquisition for the selling promoter is Rs 6.77 per share.

concentration.note: Top 10 OEM customers were 36.60% of 2025 revenue (31.72% in H1 2026). Related-party purchases were 15.18% of raw material purchases in 2025; largest supplier is group company Bonfiglioli Riduttori S.p.A.

litigation_note: No criminal proceedings against the company. Eight cheque-bounce recovery cases filed by the company total Rs 4.31 crore. Contingent liabilities were Rs 3.08 crore at June 30, 2026 (income tax Rs 2.81 crore, indirect tax Rs 0.28 crore).
strengths: Largest Indian maker of gearboxes and drives across industrial automation, off-highway mobility and wind, with 25% to 67.9% share in its segments (F&S report).
Backed by Bonfiglioli group brand and global R&D, with an India R&D centre of 119 engineers and the only Indian test lab for wind yaw and pitch drives.
Strong profit growth: PAT rose from Rs 146.67 crore in 2023 to Rs 237.87 crore in 2025 and EBITDA margin from 14.45% to 18.41%.
Debt-free with net cash of Rs 160.38 crore at Dec 2025; ROCE 34.05% and RoNW 23.96%.
Diversified across three verticals and over 930 customers; no single industry above 10% of Industry and Automation revenue.
Co-engineers with OEMs such as JCB, Hyundai, CNH, Nordex and Suzlon; seven or more of top 10 OEMs have been customers for over 10 years.
New products contributed 35.69% of 2025 revenue, showing a growing innovation pipeline.
Localised supply chain: about 70% of 2025 raw material purchases were domestic, with 215 Indian suppliers.

risks.title: Heavy dependence on promoter group for brand and technology
risks.detail: Company pays 6% of sales of licensed products to Bonfiglioli S.p.A. for the Bonfiglioli trade name and IP; any change in the relationship would hurt the business.

risks.title: Large related-party dealings
risks.detail: Related-party income was 15.59% and related-party expenses 24.83% of total income in 2025 (32.71% expenses in H1 2026); conflicts of interest possible.

risks.title: Supplier concentration with a group company
risks.detail: Related parties supplied 15.18% of 2025 purchases (19.98% in 2023); top 10 suppliers were 41.20%; no definitive agreements with many suppliers.

risks.title: Customer concentration
risks.detail: Top 10 OEM customers were 36.60% of 2025 revenue and 37.83% in H1 2025; no long-term binding agreements with all customers.

risks.title: Reliance on co-engineered products where IP stays with the group
risks.detail: Majority of revenue historically comes from co-engineered Off-Highway and Wind products whose IP is owned by the Bonfiglioli Group.

risks.title: Administrative dependence on the group
risks.detail: BSPA and group companies provide corporate and administrative services for fees; professional fees to group entities were Rs 42.78 crore in 2025.

risks.title: Offer is entirely a sale by the promoter
risks.detail: Up to 4,32,39,042 shares are sold by Bonfiglioli S.p.A. (about 23% of the company); the company receives no money, and the seller's average cost is only Rs 6.77 per share.

risks.title: Missing corporate records and input cost risk
risks.detail: Certain RoC forms and records from incorporation and early share allotments (1999 to 2001) are untraceable; raw material price rises and plant disruptions could also hit margins.

notes: Fiscal year ends Dec 31; periods are Dec-23, Dec-24, Dec-25. Figures are continuing operations (discontinued operations excluded from PAT/EPS/KPIs); company has no subsidiaries so restated financials treated as Standalone. H1 2026 and H1 2025 stubs ignored in arrays (H1 2026 revenue Rs 1131.87 crore, PAT Rs 148.58 crore, EPS 7.90). pat_margin is as reported (PAT / total income). debt_equity (borrowings/net worth) and current_ratio computed from balance sheet totals as not reported; borrowings exclude lease liabilities. EPS reflects 1:2 bonus issue of Jan 2026. cash_and_bank = cash plus other bank balances. Offer price, issue size and P/E blank in RHP; holding_post_pct derived assuming all 43,239,042 offered shares are sold; employee reservation up to 50,000 shares. Tables in Rs million converted to crore.
